concerns.decision: Reuse W, V_p,o, H_p,o, observation boundaries, and archival evidence; do not add a second world or history.
Add a revisioned policy relation over crossings, markings, authority, declassification, projection, and evidence under SEM-230.
Define governed labels and participant/policy-relative hiding; tau is a projection fact, not an intrinsic action boolean.
Reuse SEM-213 and RUN-308 order/time carriers; every claim declares total, partial, causal, simultaneous, or realized order.
Compose authenticated principal, participant authority, SEM-211 admission, policy revision, and capability checks deny-first.
Evaluate observation boundary, V_p,o, audience, markings, declassification, projection/redaction, loss, and evidence before serialization.
Keep proposal, approval, direction, intervention, handoff, override, cancellation, admission, execution, and observation distinct.
Preserve orchestration inject identity and govern participant delivery as disclosure/observation, plus intervention when it directs action/control.
Record source/result identity, rule revision, authority, markings, evidence, provenance, loss, and fresh admission for transformed actions.
Compose existing typed carriers with API-423 crossing decision/evidence records; no generic message DTO.
Extend ParticipantControlMixin, retrieval projection, RuntimeSnapshot, ControlPlaneStore, AuditEvent, and behavior histories.
Extend API-407 feature support, reject missing required semantics, and disclose bounded realization without support booleans.
Reuse existing relation bindings and conformance runners; finite probes retain finite scope and explicit nonclaims.
Adopt staged, fail-closed migration under ADR-061; legacy absence never implies a stronger policy or claim.
Publish audience-specific guidance only after authority, implementation, migration, and assurance evidence exist.

information_flow_operations.meaning: Decides whether an authenticated actor or principal has authority for the requested subject and scope.
Decides whether one governed action or crossing may proceed at the current state, order point, and policy revision.
Records an intentional non-release without transforming content or granting future disclosure.
Selects participant-visible content from an authorized source at a named observation and order point.
Suppresses governed fields or values as one projection operation while retaining the source and policy evidence.
Transforms an already governed representation and records the rule, result, markings, loss, and provenance.
Changes release authority under an explicit what, who, where, when, basis, and policy-revision decision.
Realizes an authorized release to a named participant or audience and records delivery evidence.
Changes future participant visibility under a governed state transition without rewriting prior knowledge.
Withdraws future authority or availability and records its effective order; it cannot erase prior disclosure.
Discloses unavailable fidelity, evidence, ordering, or representation rather than presenting it as security enforcement.
Records a policy-authorized lower guarantee and prevents retention of the stronger capability or relation claim.

relation_claims.definition: Low-equivalent initial states and inputs remain equivalent after participant-policy purge except at explicitly governed declassification events.
relation_claims.projection: Participant, policy identity/revision, low-equivalence and purge/declassification projection.
relation_claims.quantifiers: To be fixed by SEM-230 over states, traces, high inputs, and permitted releases.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Declared order domain plus termination, progress, timing, and concurrency sensitivity.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: Declared scheduler, environment, nondeterminism, and probability assumptions.
relation_claims.evidence_boundary: No current universal evidence; future proof or explicitly bounded model-check domain only.
explicit_nonclaims: Projected-history equality and finite leakage tests do not prove universal noninterference.

relation_claims.definition: Two recorded histories have equal participant projections for the same participant and policy revision within the compared boundary.
relation_claims.projection: Named participant, observation policy revision, redaction, order, and simultaneity projection.
relation_claims.time_and_order: The recorded order and simultaneity policy.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: The two declared run contexts; no scheduler universalization.
relation_claims.evidence_boundary: Compared histories and their projection/evidence records.
explicit_nonclaims: No future-behavior, noninterference, trace-equivalence, or bisimulation claim.

relation_claims.definition: Every projected trace of one named model is admitted by another under a declared direction and projection.
relation_claims.projection: Named carrier, participant projection, label hiding, and policy revision.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Must name sequential, timed, or partial-order trace semantics.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: Must quantify schedulers and environments explicitly.
relation_claims.evidence_boundary: Currently bounded probes only; proof remains future.
explicit_nonclaims: Passing conformance probes does not prove trace inclusion.

relation_claims.definition: Each source step is matched by a target step sequence under a state relation and declared hidden-action treatment.
relation_claims.projection: State relation, labels, tau closure, participant policy revision.
relation_claims.quantifiers: Future universal step obligation over reachable states.
explicit_nonclaims: Trace samples and schema validity do not establish simulation.

relation_claims.definition: Concrete participant-control state preserves the abstract observation and operation obligations through a declared abstraction relation.
relation_claims.projection: Abstract/concrete state mapping and participant observation projection.
relation_claims.quantifiers: Future universal operation and reachable-state obligation.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Operation ordering and atomicity must be declared.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: Interference and environment assumptions must be declared.
explicit_nonclaims: Carrier round trips do not prove data refinement.

relation_claims.definition: Both labelled systems match every step bidirectionally with no hidden-action elision.
relation_claims.projection: Declared state relation and exact observable/hidden label partition.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Transition-system semantics with declared divergence and timing treatment.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: All relevant branches under declared environment/scheduler assumptions.
explicit_nonclaims: Matching one trace or passing bounded probes is not strong bisimulation.

relation_claims.definition: Both labelled systems match visible behavior bidirectionally through governed hidden-action closure.
relation_claims.projection: Declared tau set, closure, divergence, participant policy, and state relation.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Transition, divergence, timing, and partial-order treatment must be declared.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: All relevant branches under declared environment/scheduler assumptions.
explicit_nonclaims: Visible trace equality is not weak bisimulation.

relation_claims.definition: Two worlds are indistinguishable to a participant under a governed information-state model and local history.
relation_claims.projection: Participant local history, policy revision, observation and recall model.
relation_claims.time_and_order: Information sets at declared order points.
relation_claims.scheduler_and_environment: Knowledge model must state environment and scheduler observability.
relation_claims.evidence_boundary: No current governed epistemic model or proof.
explicit_nonclaims: Equal observations alone do not establish knowledge or indistinguishability.
